newsitem.title: MACAU: Portugal's Sampaio to proceed with China visit.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's Sampaio to proceed with China visit.

text.p: Portuguese President Jorge Sampaio plans to proceed as planned with his visit to China next week despite the death of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, his press adviser said on Thursday.

"The visit will go ahead as planned, except for some minor protocol changes required because of the official mourning in China," Antonio Manuel told Reuters. Sampaio arrived in Macau for a six-day official visit to the Portuguese-administered territory on Tuesday and was due to leave for Beijing on Sunday.
He offered his condolences on Deng's death, who he described as an "eminent statesman" who captured a major place in 20th century Chinese history.
The Macau government ordered Portuguese flags to fly at half mast but it was business as usual in the enclave.
Gambling in Macau's nine casinos continued unabated and schools and businesses were open.
Macau will revert to China on December 20, 1999, after nearly 450 years of Portuguese administration.
Macau governor General Vasco Rocha Vieira extended his condolences in a letter to China's president Jiang Zemin.
Vieira called Deng a "statesman of unmatched dimension who would be remembered in history as the great driving force behind the modernisation of China".
Deng died late on Wednesday from respiratory failure. He was 92.
